reason: Start with the arterial route carrying blood toward tissues.
expectation: I expect the lining and thick wall to form an artery, though its connections may need further steps.

alternatives.reason: Capillaries are central to exchange, but I’ll start with the outward route.
The vein is also needed, but I’ll build the arterial side first.

effect: The artery is built, with an elastic wall that stretches and recoils; the exchange and return vessels remain.
reaction: The pulse and rest comparison makes the wall’s role clearer.
reason: Build the capillary network next to connect the arterial route to tissue exchange.
expectation: I expect endothelial cells to line the support sleeves and form capillaries; they may still need connections to the other vessels.

alternatives.reason: The venous route is also needed, but capillaries come between arteries and veins.

effect: The capillary bed is ready for exchange and can now be connected to the artery.
reaction: The thin walls make the exchange role clear, though the picture description is brief.
reason: Connect the arterial vessels to the capillary bed as the next part of the route.
expectation: I expect a connected arterial-to-capillary route that will still need a venous return.

alternatives.reason: The vein is also needed, but I want to connect the existing vessels first.

effect: The arterial route now branches through arterioles into capillaries near tissue cells; a venous return remains to be built.
reaction: The parallel branches make the distribution role clearer.
reason: Build the vein for the return route; this is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect a lined venous vessel, possibly still needing valves and a connection to the capillary bed.

effect: The lined vein is built; it can now receive valves before joining the route.
reaction: The thin wall contrasts clearly with the artery, though the result is brief.
reason: Add the valve folds to the vein; this is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect a vein with valves that help prevent backflow, still needing connection to the capillary bed.

effect: The vein now has valves, and the picture shows how limb-muscle compression helps move blood toward the heart.
reaction: The forward and backward arrows make the valves’ purpose clear.
reason: Connect the exchange bed to venous return; this is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect a continuous route from arteries through capillaries to veins.

effect: The final connection completes the systemic route from arteries through capillaries to veins and clarifies that arteries carry blood away from the heart and veins return it.
reaction: The completed route is a clear summary, though the final picture description is brief.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding venous valves was most worthwhile: the planned muscle-compression and flow-arrow comparison explains how valves help prevent backflow.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making the thin-walled vein felt least substantial: its brief picture largely repeated the information in the item title.

surprise.text: The valve result clarified that contracting limb muscle can help propel venous blood toward the heart, not just that valves block backflow.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, although several were the only offered combination, so they involved little decision-making.

continue.text: I would continue to see how the vessel route connects to the heart and circulation; the branching and valve illustrations gave the structures understandable jobs.
